configuration_map: All points are collinear on segment AB in the order A--D--C--B. Point C divides AB in extreme and mean ratio with AC the greater segment (AC/AB ~ 0.618). Point D bisects AB (AD = DB = AB/2). Since AC/AB > 1/2, D falls between A and C. No off-line points are constructed. The entire proof after the initial construction operates algebraically on lengths and rectangular areas using Book 2 identities (2.1, 2.4) and the mean proportional property (6.17).
pass_reason: The proof makes only trivial spatial claims (collinear points on a single line segment), all mutually consistent. The core reasoning is entirely algebraic — area identities from Book 2 applied to lengths — with no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior arguments, and no geometric configurations that could produce contradictions.
